mainTopic: Learning the laws of פסח before the חג, אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה, and why ביטול חמץ is done at the time of בדיקה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of how early we start learning the laws of פסח. The תנא קמא says thirty days, because משה taught the laws of פסח שני on פסח ראשון. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rejects that proof and says two weeks. After one source is dropped, the גמרא proves through a גזירה שוה from 'במדבר סיני' that משה taught the laws of פסח on ראש חודש ניסן. That raises a question: why is the ניסן speech written after the אייר speech? The answer is אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה. רב פפא limits this rule to separate topics, and proves from the rules of כלל ופרט that within one topic the written order is exact. Then a new topic begins: רב rules that one who does בדיקת חמץ must also do ביטול. רבא explains that this is a decree, in case he later finds a nice loaf after the sixth hour, when he can no longer nullify it. ביטול is fixed at night with the בדיקה so that he will not forget.

steps.title: The source for thirty days: משה on פסח ראשון
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns the thirty-day rule from משה, who taught the laws of פסח שני on the day of פסח ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because משה stood on the first פסח and warned about the second פסח, as it says: 'Let the children of Israel make the פסח in its time.' And it is written: 'And there were men who were impure from a dead person.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the question on the previous amud: what is the reason of the תנא קמא, who says to start learning the laws of פסח thirty days ahead? The answer is that משה himself taught a festival's laws thirty days before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the 14th of ניסן, which was פסח ראשון, some people were טמא מת and could not bring the קרבן. משה then taught them about פסח שני, which falls on the 14th of אייר, exactly thirty days later. So learning a חג's laws thirty days early follows משה's own model.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (regular) פסח, on 14 ניסן
The make-up פסח, on 14 אייר, for those who missed the first
Warns, instructs about the laws
Impure from contact with a dead body
And it is written (bringing a second פסוק)

phrases.english: For Moses was standing at the first Pesach,
and warning about the second Pesach,
phrases.notes: The second Pesach is thirty days later.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Let the children of Israel perform'
the Pesach at its appointed time' (Bamidbar 9:2),
and it is written: 'And there were people'
who were impure due to a dead body' (Bamidbar 9:6).
phrases.notes: This opens the Torah's section about פסח שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהֲרֵי מֹשֶׁה עוֹמֵד בְּפֶסַח רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'מאי טעמא דתנא קמא', which was asked on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source for learning the laws of a חג thirty days in advance?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה taught the laws of פסח שני on פסח ראשון, thirty days earlier.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rejects the proof
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says משה taught about פסח שני only because he was already discussing פסח, so no general rule can be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would tell you: since he was already speaking about matters of פסח, he finished all the matters of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would push away the proof for thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that the thirty-day gap was a coincidence of the topic. משה was teaching פסח anyway, so he completed the whole subject, including פסח שני. That was not a deliberate model of 'learn thirty days ahead.'

keyTerms.meaning: Since he was already speaking about
Matters of פסח
He completes them, finishes the topic
Would say to you (a defense of a position)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אָמַר לָךְ:
phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel could say to you:
Since he was speaking about matters of Pesach,
he completed all the matters of Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof for thirty days. It does not reject the idea of learning before the חג.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The timing came from finishing a topic already being discussed, so it sets no deliberate thirty-day rule.

steps.title: What is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the positive source of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's two-week rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Now that we know why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rejects thirty days, the גמרא asks where his own two weeks comes from, and the answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rejecting the other side's proof is not enough. A position also needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason/source?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rejection of the thirty-day proof to the source of the two-week view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for learning the laws of פסח two weeks in advance.

steps.title: The source for two weeks: משה on ראש חודש ניסן
steps.stepSummary: משה taught the laws of the קרבן פסח on ראש חודש ניסן, two weeks before the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because משה stood on ראש חודש and warned about פסח, as it says: 'This month shall be for you the head of months.' And it is written: 'Speak to the whole congregation of Israel, saying: on the tenth of this month they shall take for themselves, each man, a lamb for his father's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns from משה teaching the פסח laws in פרשת החודש. According to this reading, that teaching happened on ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'החודש הזה לכם' suggests משה was speaking at the start of the month. The following פסוקים teach the laws of the קרבן פסח, brought on the 14th. From the 1st to the 14th is about two weeks, which matches the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the month
'This month shall be for you' (שמות יב:ב)
On the tenth of the month
A lamb for each family

phrases.english: For Moses was standing on the New Moon,
and warning about the Pesach,
as it is stated: 'This month shall be for you the beginning of months' (Shemos 12:2),

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״דַּבְּרוּ אֶל כׇּל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר
phrases.english: and it is written: 'Speak to the entire congregation of Israel, saying:'
'On the tenth of this month'

phrases.aramaic: וְיִקְחוּ לָהֶם אִישׁ שֶׂה לְבֵית אָבוֹת וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: 'they shall take for them every man a lamb for their fathers' houses, etc.' (Shemos 12:3).

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהֲרֵי מֹשֶׁה עוֹמֵד בְּרֹאשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה taught the laws of פסח on ראש חודש ניסן, two weeks before פסח.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sources. The thirty days comes from פסח ראשון to פסח שני (step 1). The two weeks comes from ראש חודש ניסן to the 14th of ניסן (this step).

steps.title: How do we know משה spoke on ראש חודש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that משה's speech took place on the first of the month.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know he was standing at the beginning of the month? Maybe he was standing on the fourth of the month or the fifth of the month?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the source of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The פסוק says 'this month,' but that does not prove משה spoke on day one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole two-week count depends on the speech happening on ראש חודש. If משה spoke on the 4th or 5th, the gap to the 14th is only about ten days, and the proof for two weeks falls apart. The גמרא never defends this source. In the next step (step 6) it says 'אלא' and replaces it with a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we know)?
At the beginning of the month
Perhaps
He was standing

phrases.english: From where do we know that he was standing at the beginning of the month?
Perhaps on the fourth of the month
or on the fifth of the month he was standing?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דִּבְרֵישׁ יַרְחָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption about timing in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that משה gave the פסח instructions on ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים do not state the date of the speech. Without proof that it was the 1st of the month, the two-week count is unsupported.

steps.title: A new verse shows משה taught פסח laws in the first month
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שימי, in the name of רבינא, brings a new source: משה was told about the פסח in the first month of the second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר שימי said in the name of רבינא: we learn it from here. 'And ה׳ spoke to משה in the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year, in the first month.' And it is written: 'Let the children of Israel make the פסח at its set time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier source and brings a new verse to prove that משה taught the laws of פסח two weeks before the holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says this speech about the פסח happened 'in the first month,' which is ניסן. Since the פסח is brought on the 14th, the speech came before the holiday. That supports רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's two-week rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
From here. It points to the new source.
In the first month (ניסן)
At its set time

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Shimi said
in the name of Ravina: it is learned from here:
phrases.notes: A new source replaces the one challenged in Step 5.

phrases.english: "And God spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai
in the second year, in the first month"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is במדבר ט:א.

phrases.english: and it is written: "Let the children of Israel make
the Pesach at its set time."
phrases.notes: This is במדבר ט:ב, and this speech is all about the פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שִׁימִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source from Step 4, which was challenged in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: במדבר ט:א-ב shows that משה taught the laws of פסח in ניסן, before the 14th.

steps.title: How do we know this speech was on the first of the month?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question as before: perhaps the speech was on the 4th or 5th of ניסן, not the 1st.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, how do we know he stood and spoke on the first of the month? Maybe he spoke on the 4th of the month or the 5th of the month?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new source. The verse says 'first month,' but it does not say 'first day.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove a full two weeks, we need the speech to be on day 1. If it was on day 4 or 5, it was less than two weeks before פסח. The word 'too' (נמי) shows this is the same challenge as Step 5, now aimed at the new verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too. The same question is asked again.
At the beginning of the month, ראש חודש
He was standing (speaking)

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, מִמַּאי דִּבְרֵישׁ יַרְחָא קָאֵי?
phrases.english: Here too, from where do we know he was standing at the beginning of the month?
Perhaps on the fourth of the month
or on the fifth of the month he was standing?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי מִמַּאי דִּבְרֵישׁ יַרְחָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new source from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the speech in במדבר ט:א was on ראש חודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'The first month' does not say which day. Without day 1, the two-week count is not proven.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from 'מדבר סיני' proves the speech was on ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק links the two verses that say 'במדבר סיני.' One verse is clearly dated to the 1st of the month, so the other is on the 1st too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we learn 'wilderness' from 'wilderness.' It is written here, 'in the wilderness of Sinai,' and it is written there, 'And ה׳ spoke to משה in the wilderness of Sinai, in the אהל מועד, on the first of the second month.' Just as there it was on ראש חודש, so too here it was on ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge with a word-link (גזירה שוה) between two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: במדבר א:א says 'במדבר סיני' and gives the date: the first of the month. Our verse (במדבר ט:א) uses the same words but gives no day. The shared words teach that our speech was also on the first of the month, so the full two weeks is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned) from. This is the language of a גזירה שוה.
Learning a law by linking the same word in two verses
Just as there, so too here
On the first of the month

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is derived: "wilderness" from "wilderness."
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word shows up in both places, so we learn one from the other.

phrases.english: It is written here: "in the wilderness of Sinai,"
and it is written there: "And God spoke to Moses
in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting,
on the first of the second month."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is במדבר א:א.

phrases.english: Just as there it was on the New Moon,
so too here it was on the New Moon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אַתְיָא מִדְבָּר מִמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: גזירה שוה that supplies the missing date
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The speech in ניסן could have been on any day, such as the 4th or 5th.
steps.terutzMaskana: The speech was on ראש חודש ניסן, a full two weeks before פסח.

steps.title: Why is the ניסן speech written after the אייר speech?
steps.stepSummary: If the ניסן speech came first in time, the Torah should have written it before the אייר speech at the start of ספר במדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the Torah write first what happened in the first month, and afterward write what happened in the second month!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem that comes from the answer just given: the order of the verses does not match the order of the events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 places our speech on 1 ניסן and the speech in במדבר א on 1 אייר. Yet the Torah writes the אייר speech in chapter 1 and the ניסן speech later, in chapter 9. Why is the earlier event written later?

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it write. This is a challenge about how the Torah is written.
First
And afterward

phrases.english: Then let it write first the matter of the first month,
and afterward let it write the matter of the second month.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִיכְתּוֹב בְּרֵישָׁא דְּחֹדֶשׁ רִאשׁוֹן וַהֲדַר נִיכְתּוֹב דְּחֹדֶשׁ שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grows out of the answer in Step 8, which fixed the dates of the two speeches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the verses in ספר במדבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An event from ניסן should be written before an event from אייר, but the Torah writes it after.

steps.title: The Torah is not always written in time order
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that this case shows אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה: the Torah's order is not always the order in which things happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר תחליפא said in the name of רב: this teaches that there is no 'earlier' and 'later' in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by saying the Torah does not always follow time order, and this case proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order problem is not a mistake. It shows a general principle: an event that happened earlier can be written later in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches. A general rule is learned from this case.
There is no 'earlier and later' in the Torah. The Torah is not always in time order.

steps.confusionAlert: This does NOT mean the Torah has no order at all. רב פפא is about to limit this rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Menashiya bar Tachlifa said in the name of Rav:
That is to say,
there is no earlier and later in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת אֵין מוּקְדָּם וּמְאוּחָר בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the order question from Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general principle about how the Torah is ordered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah must be written in time order.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah can write an earlier event after a later one.
steps.whyThisMatters: אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה is a famous principle that is used all over שס and in מפרשים like רש״י.

steps.title: The rule applies only between separate topics
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the rule: it applies only between two separate topics. Within one topic, what is written first happened first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: we only said this about two separate topics. But within one topic, what is written earlier is earlier, and what is written later is later.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows רב's rule so that it does not go too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ניסן speech and the אייר speech are two different topics, so the Torah could put them out of time order. Inside a single topic, the order of the verses is exact and can be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this about. This limits an earlier statement.
Two separate topics
One topic

steps.whatToRemember: אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה applies only between separate topics. Within one topic, the written order is the true order.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We said this only with regard to two separate matters,
but within one matter,
what is written earlier is earlier,
and what is written later is later.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בִּתְרֵי עִנְיָינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the principle stated in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Time order is not required between separate topics, but within one topic the written order is the real order.

steps.title: Proof from כלל ופרט that order matters within one topic
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא proves his limit. The rule of כלל ופרט only works if the order of words inside one passage is fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, then the rule 'when a general term is followed by a specific term, the general term includes only what is in the specific term' would fail. Maybe it is really a specific term followed by a general term!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a proof that order matters inside one topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of learning Torah treat כלל ופרט (general, then specific) differently from פרט וכלל (specific, then general), and the two give different results. If the order inside one passage could not be trusted, we could never tell which one we have. Since everyone uses the כלל ופרט rule, order within one topic must count.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so. This introduces a proof by showing what would go wrong otherwise.
A general term followed by a specific term. Only the specific item is included.
A specific term followed by a general term. Everything is included.

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's limit rests on the rules of reading the Torah: כלל ופרט only works if the order of words inside one passage is fixed.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,

phrases.aramaic: ״כְּלָל וּפְרָט — אֵין בַּכְּלָל אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁבַּפְּרָט״,
phrases.english: "A generalization and a detail: the generalization includes only what is in the detail,"
phrases.notes: One of the 13 rules of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: perhaps it is a detail and a generalization!
phrases.notes: פרט וכלל gives the opposite result: the general term adds everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's limit from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: Order is fixed within a single topic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule of כלל ופרט, which depends on the order of the words.

steps.title: A second proof from detail followed by generalization
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that the rule of פרט וכלל also needs the order inside one passage to be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: there is the rule 'a detail followed by a generalization: the generalization adds to the detail.' If order did not matter, maybe it is really a generalization followed by a detail!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second proof, just like the one in step 12. This time it uses the rule of פרט וכלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרט וכלל, a detail and then a general term, widens the law. כלל ופרט, a general term and then a detail, narrows it. If the order of words inside one passage were not fixed, we could never know which rule to use. So inside one topic, what is written first must really come first.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: adds another point
A detail followed by a general term
The general term adds to the detail and widens the law
Perhaps / maybe

phrases.english: And furthermore,
"A detail followed by a generalization:
phrases.notes: This is one of the 13 ways of reading the Torah

phrases.english: the generalization becomes an addition to the detail",
perhaps it is really a generalization followed by a detail!
phrases.notes: That reading would give the opposite result: narrowing instead of widening

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, פְּרָט וּכְלָל נַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל מוּסָף עַל הַפְּרָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, matching proof to step 12's proof from כלל ופרט.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's limit: within one topic, the written order is the real order.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule of פרט וכלל, which only works if word order inside a passage is fixed.

steps.title: Challenge: then order should matter across two topics too
steps.stepSummary: If כלל ופרט depends on fixed order, then for the view that applies it even to far-apart verses, order should be fixed across two topics as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the rule should apply even across two topics! This works for the one who says: a generalization and a detail that are far apart from each other cannot be used as כלל ופרט. But for the one who says they can be used, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's limit. It says his logic seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says a כלל and a פרט far apart in the Torah can still be read together. If they can be far apart, they might sit in two different topics. Then order would have to be fixed even across topics. That goes against אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
Two separate topics or passages
This works fine (for one view)
Far apart from each other in the Torah
We learn from it / we apply the rule
What can be said? The problem stands for this view

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against the rule of כלל ופרט itself. It only asks whether רב פפא's logic forces order to be fixed even across two topics.

phrases.english: If so,
then even across two topics as well!
phrases.notes: Order should be fixed there too

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says:
"A generalization and a detail that are far apart from each other:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ בִּכְלָל וּפְרָט״, שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: we do not apply כלל ופרט to them." That is fine,
but for the one who says "we do apply it,"
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ בִּתְרֵי עִנְיָינֵי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proofs of steps 12-13 by saying they prove too much.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's limit that אין מוקדם ומאוחר still applies between two topics.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a far-apart כלל ופרט works, order must be fixed even between distant verses, which may be in two topics. That would cancel אין מוקדם ומאוחר.

steps.title: Far-apart verses count only within one topic
steps.stepSummary: Even the view that applies a far-apart כלל ופרט only does so within the same topic. Across two topics, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even for the one who says 'we apply it,' that is only within one topic. But across two topics, we do not apply it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows the view that allows far-apart verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view of דנין lets the כלל and the פרט be far apart, but only if both deal with the same subject. Across two different topics, nobody applies כלל ופרט. So רב פפא's limit stands: order is fixed only within one topic.

keyTerms.meaning: This only applies to: limits a rule
One topic
We do not apply the rule

steps.whatToRemember: אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה applies between separate topics. Within one topic, even if the verses are far apart, the written order is the real order.

phrases.english: Even for the one who says "we do apply it,"
that is only within one topic.
But across two topics, we do not apply it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דָּנִין, הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּחַד עִנְיָינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the opposing view (דנין) to one topic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The view of דנין seemed to apply a far-apart כלל ופרט anywhere, even across topics.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only applies within one topic, so order between separate topics stays unfixed.

steps.title: One who searches for חמץ must also cancel it
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: after בדיקת חמץ, a person must also do ביטול חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: one who searches for חמץ must also cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב rules that searching for חמץ is not enough, and the person must also cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביטול means declaring that any חמץ you own counts as nothing, like dust. רב adds this on top of the search. This opens a new discussion, since the search should seem to take care of everything.

keyTerms.meaning: One who searches (for חמץ)
Must cancel it, declaring his חמץ worthless

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the practice of saying כל חמירא after the search the night before פסח.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One who searches must cancel (his chametz).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב הַבּוֹדֵק צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic; not connected to the discussion of order in the Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After בדיקת חמץ, one must also do ביטול.

steps.title: Why is cancelling needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ביטול is needed after the search. This sets up the next move, where reasons will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The search should remove all the חמץ, so a second step seems unneeded. The גמרא wants to know what problem ביטול solves.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 16's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What problem remains after the search that makes ביטול necessary?

steps.title: Not because of crumbs, since crumbs do not matter
steps.stepSummary: The first suggested reason, leftover crumbs, is rejected because crumbs are not important anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of crumbs he may have missed, those are not important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reason, crumbs left after the search, and pushes it away right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small crumbs are worthless on their own, so they already count as nothing. Cancelling them would add nothing. So ביטול must be needed for some other reason, which the גמרא will look for next.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion
Crumbs
They are not important; they count as nothing

phrases.english: If you say it is because of crumbs,
they are not important!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא מִשּׁוּם פֵּירוּרִין הָא לָא חֲשִׁיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first answer to step 17's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the crumbs reason, not רב's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Crumbs are already worthless, so ביטול would add nothing for them.

steps.title: Maybe crumbs are important because they are guarded with the house
steps.stepSummary: A possible push-back against step 18: crumbs might count as significant because the owner guards them along with his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: since the crumbs are guarded along with his house, they are significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible argument to save the crumbs reason that was just rejected. It suggests the crumbs matter because they are protected inside the owner's guarded house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said crumbs are unimportant, so they don't need ביטול. This step argues back: a person guards his house, and everything inside is guarded too. If they are guarded, maybe they count as important.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible argument)
Is guarded / protected
Along with, by way of
They are significant / important

phrases.english: And if you will say:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דִּמְינַטַּר לְהוּ אַגַּב בֵּיתֵיהּ — חֲשִׁיבִי,
phrases.english: Since they are guarded along with his house, they are significant,
phrases.notes: The owner guards his house, so the crumbs inside are guarded too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כֵּיוָן דִּמְינַטַּר לְהוּ אַגַּב בֵּיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 18 by offering a reason why crumbs might be significant after all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 18 that crumbs are unimportant.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Things protected inside a guarded house might gain importance, so crumbs would need ביטול.

steps.title: Leftover figs and grapes show that guarding does not make items important
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that leftover fruit in a guarded field is ownerless when the owner doesn't care about it. So guarding a place does not make unwanted items significant.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: Leftover figs at the end of the season, while the owner guards his field because of the grapes; leftover grapes, while he guards his field because of the cucumbers and gourds. When the owner cares about them, they are forbidden because of theft and require מעשר. When the owner does not care about them, they are permitted (no theft) and exempt from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the argument in step 19 by quoting a ברייתא about leftover fruit in a guarded field. Fruit the owner doesn't care about is ownerless, even though the field around it is guarded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field is guarded only for the new crop, not for the poor leftovers. The ברייתא says the leftovers' status depends on whether the owner cares about them (מקפיד), not on whether they sit in a guarded area. Crumbs are the same: the house is guarded, but nobody cares about the crumbs, so they stay unimportant.

keyTerms.meaning: The last, poor-quality figs left at the end of the season
Cares about, is particular about
Theft
Tithe; ownerless produce is exempt
Cucumbers and gourds

steps.confusionAlert: The field IS guarded. The point is that guarding it for a different crop does not make the leftover fruit important. Only the owner's caring (מקפיד) decides.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
Leftover figs at the end of the season,
and he guards his field because of the grapes.
Leftover grapes at the end of the season,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְשַׁמֵּר שָׂדֵהוּ מִפְּנֵי מִקְשָׁאוֹת וּמִפְּנֵי מִדְלָעוֹת,
phrases.english: and he guards his field because of the cucumbers and because of the gourds,
when the owner cares about them,
they are forbidden because of theft, and they require tithing.

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מַקְפִּיד עֲלֵיהֶן —
phrases.english: When the owner does not care about them,

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּרִין מִשּׁוּם גֵּזֶל, וּפְטוּרִין מִשּׁוּם מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: they are permitted as far as theft goes, and exempt from tithing.
phrases.notes: Exempt because they are treated as ownerless (הפקר).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: סוֹפֵי תְאֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the argument of step 19 using a ברייתא, which keeps step 18's conclusion in place.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that guarding the house makes the crumbs significant.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being in a guarded area does not create importance. Only the owner's caring (מקפיד) does, and nobody cares about crumbs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes off the crumbs explanation completely and sends the גמרא looking for a new reason for רב's rule.

steps.title: רבא: a decree in case he finds a nice loaf he cares about
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ביטול is required as a rabbinic precaution. The person might find a fine loaf he values and hesitate to destroy it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a decree, in case he finds a fine loaf and his mind is set on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the question of step 17: why ביטול is needed after בדיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is no longer small crumbs but a nice, valuable loaf that the search missed. Because he likes it, he may hesitate to burn it and end up owning חמץ on פסח. Doing ביטול ahead of time protects him in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic protective decree
Lest, in case
A fine, high-quality loaf or cake
His mind is on it; he values it

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is a decree, lest he find a fine loaf
and his mind is set on it.
phrases.notes: He values it, so he may not want to destroy it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִמְצָא גְּלוּסְקָא יָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected crumbs reason with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ביטול is a precaution in case he finds a valuable loaf he cares about and fails to destroy it.

steps.title: Why not just nullify the loaf when he finds it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: if he finds a loaf, he can do ביטול at that moment, so why require it in advance?
steps.simpleTranslation: But when he finds it, let him nullify it then!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reason. Nullifying the loaf when it is found would seem to be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only fear is a loaf found later, he can declare it ownerless the moment he finds it. Then there is no need for a ביטול in advance right after בדיקה.

keyTerms.meaning: You find it
Let him nullify it (ביטול)

phrases.english: But when he finds it, let him nullify it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ לְבַטְּלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reason in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's decree requiring ביטול in advance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nullifying at the time of finding would solve the problem, so the advance ביטול seems unnecessary.

steps.title: He may find it after it is forbidden, when ביטול no longer works
steps.stepSummary: He might find the loaf after the sixth hour. By then the חמץ is not legally his, so he can no longer nullify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will find it after the time it becomes forbidden. Then it is not in his possession, and he cannot nullify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. A loaf found too late can't be nullified, so ביטול must be done earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביטול works only on something you own. Once חמץ becomes forbidden, it has no value and is not legally his, so he has no power to give it up. Yet he still breaks the prohibition if he keeps it, which is why ביטול must happen before that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
After the time it becomes forbidden
In his legal possession / ownership
He cannot nullify

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not in his possession' does not mean he is off the hook. He still transgresses if he keeps it. He just loses the ability to nullify it.

phrases.english: Perhaps you will find it after it becomes forbidden,
and it is not standing in his possession,
and he cannot nullify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ לְבָתַר אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing limitation: nullifying when found does not always work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He can always nullify the loaf when he finds it.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he finds it after the sixth hour, it is not legally his, so ביטול is impossible. That is why ביטול must be done in advance.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: חמץ after the sixth hour is treated as his though it is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a pit in the public domain and חמץ after the sixth hour are not legally owned, yet the Torah treats them as if they were. This supports step 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעזר said: Two things are not in a person's possession, yet the Torah treated them as if they were in his possession. They are: a pit in the public domain, and חמץ from the sixth hour and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for step 23's claim that חמץ after the sixth hour is not in his possession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ after the sixth hour is forbidden for any benefit, so it has no value and is not truly his. That is why he can't nullify it. Still, the Torah holds him responsible for it, just as a person who digs a pit in public property is responsible for the damage it causes.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse (Torah) made them
As if in his possession
A pit in the public domain
From the sixth hour (midday of the 14th of ניסן) and onward

steps.whatToRemember: ביטול must be done before the sixth hour, because afterward the חמץ is not legally his and can't be nullified, yet he is still responsible for it. This is רבא's reason for רב's rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why ביטול must be done before the חמץ becomes forbidden (the sixth hour). After that point it no longer works, because the חמץ is not legally his.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים אֵינָן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Two things are not in a person's possession,
yet the Torah made them as if they were in his possession,
and these are they: a pit in the public domain,
phrases.notes: The digger pays for damages even though the land is not his.

phrases.english: and chametz from the sixth hour and onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים אֵינָן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 23's claim that חמץ after the sixth hour is not his.
steps.raayaObject: Step 23's claim that after the sixth hour חמץ is not in his possession and can't be nullified.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's teaching that חמץ after the sixth hour is treated by the Torah as his, though it is not truly his.

steps.title: Why not nullify in the fourth or fifth hour?
steps.stepSummary: If ביטול only has to happen before the sixth hour, the person could do it in the fourth or fifth hour of the morning. Why require it at night?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him nullify it in the fourth hour, or let him nullify it in the fifth hour!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the timing of ביטול. The deadline is the sixth hour, so why not nullify in the morning, still before the deadline?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 explained that ביטול is needed before the sixth hour. After that point the חמץ is not legally his, and he can no longer nullify it. But that only proves ביטול must come before the sixth hour. It does not prove it must happen as early as the night of בדיקה. The fourth and fifth hours still meet the deadline, so the early requirement looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him nullify it
In the fourth hour of the day
In the fifth hour of the day

phrases.english: Then let him nullify it in the fourth hour,
phrases.notes: The hours are counted from the start of the day on י״ד ניסן.

phrases.english: or let him nullify it in the fifth hour?
phrases.notes: Both of these hours are still before the sixth-hour deadline.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִיבַטְּלֵיהּ בְּאַרְבַּע, וְנִיבַטְּלֵיהּ בְּחָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 24 supported the sixth-hour deadline, the גמרא now asks why ביטול must happen so much earlier than that deadline.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement to do ביטול on the night of the fourteenth, at the time of בדיקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sixth-hour deadline only requires ביטול before the sixth hour. The fourth or fifth hour would satisfy that deadline, so the night requirement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Those hours are not a set time, so he might forget
steps.stepSummary: The fourth hour is neither the time the חמץ becomes forbidden nor the time it is destroyed. Because it is not a marked moment, the person might neglect it and never nullify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is not the time of the prohibition and not the time of the removal, perhaps he will be negligent and will not nullify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that waiting until the morning is risky. Nothing special happens at that hour to remind the person, so he might forget to do ביטול at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People remember to do something when it is tied to a clear moment or action. At night the person is already doing בדיקה, so the ביטול is attached to that event. The fourth and fifth hours are 'in-between' times, with no prohibition starting and no burning taking place. So the חכמים set ביטול at night together with בדיקה, when it will not be forgotten.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of the prohibition, when the חמץ becomes forbidden
The time of removal, when the חמץ is destroyed
Perhaps he will be negligent

steps.whatToRemember: ביטול must happen before the sixth hour, because after that he cannot nullify. It is done at night, at the time of בדיקה, because a fixed occasion keeps him from forgetting. An 'in-between' hour in the morning could easily be neglected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reason for the practical custom of saying כל חמירא right after בדיקת חמץ at night.

phrases.english: Since it is not the time of the prohibition
phrases.notes: The חמץ has not yet become forbidden at that hour.

phrases.english: and it is not the time of the removal,
phrases.notes: Nor is it the time when the חמץ is burned or destroyed.

phrases.english: perhaps he will be negligent and will not nullify it.
phrases.notes: Nothing marks the moment, so he may forget entirely.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו זְמַן אִיסּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step directly answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical precaution: concern that he will forget
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any time before the sixth hour should be good enough for ביטול.
steps.terutzMaskana: ביטול is fixed at night together with בדיקה, because the morning hours are not a marked time and he might forget.
